description:
Letter from Ramla, from Shelomo b. Yehuda, gaʾon of the Jerusalem yeshiva, in Ramla, to his son Avraham in Fustat. Dating: 21 Iyyar 4789 (Wednesday, 7 May 1029; Gil, based on the mention of 20 Iyyar as a Tuesday, which limits the options to 1029, 1036 and 1043; Gil chooses 1029 on internal grounds). Describing in great detail the economic and other calamities that haunted Palestine in this period. 

Shelomo b. Yehuda has come down from Jerusalem to Ramla at the community's request and finds himself entangled in conflict among them, labor that requires delicacy but provides no reward. He reports a deadlock over the market office (sūq), possibly the kosher butcher concession (?): the remnant of the community, most of them too poor to pay even a cantor, resolved to give the concession to the son of the shelishi (the third ranking member of the yeshiva), but he would not take up the position, and there was no one else — the sons of Shelomo ha-Kohen gaʾon, Yosef and Eliyyahu, will come down only on terms that guarantee them profit, and there is none to be had. He acknowledges the arrival of a letter from Abū Sahl (Gi: Menashshe ha-Kohen b. Avraham, his son-in-law) enclosing a payment order for Abū l-Sirrī b. Qandarī or Qundarī, which he has passed to Abū l-Ḥasan ʿAllūn b. Mūsā, even though payment was not due for another month.

The rest is distress and politics. He describes his own destitution — he survived the difficult winter, and had sold household goods and clothing the previous year; most of the land remains unsown; and there is nothing to sell in Ramla. He says he is staying in Ramla mainly because in Jerusalem, the creditors (of the yeshiva? of the Jewish community there?) come only to him. Mawhūb the blind, Abū l-Faḍl, and Mubārak b. Ṣemaḥ are in prison for debt and the rest are under demand; he has asked Jāsūs al-Maghribī to see to his family's needs in Jerusalem, though they do not want the help. He refuses on grounds of religious scruple (shubha fī dīnī) his son's suggestion that he claim the income (or fees and perquisites) formerly attached to the leadership in Fustat (rusūm kānat li-l-riyāsa bi-Miṣr), saying he doesn't know by what means his predecessors held them and will not be answerable for a transgression. He instructs Avraham to approach Efrayim b. Shemarya, "the banner of the Rabbanites today," on behalf of the debt prisoners and reproaches Abū Naṣr (Gil: Ḥesed b. Sahl al-Tustarī), a man with access to the government, for the ineffectiveness of earlier appeals. Against a ruling barring the use of waqf/heqdesh funds in Fustat to free the prisoners, he cites the precedent of predecessors who spent consecrated money on repairing the synagogue and acquiring two dwellings. He asks about a woollen badan (short outer garment with no or short sleeves) to be sold in Egypt for the benefit of Sahlān b. Avraham, the rosh kalla. He reports outstanding sums from Sicily and Tyre and warns his son urgently to keep clear of the rift between Rabbanites and Qaraites in Fustat, "for the umma today is ailing and requires gentle handling, as an invalid is handled gently" (v23). 

In addition to the edition by Gil, there is also one by Goitein in Shalem 1 (1974), 34–44.

description_he: מכתב מרמלה, מאת רב שלמה בן יהודה אל בנו אברהם בפוסטאט, מאי 1029 (לפי גיל), המתאר בפירוט רב את הצרות הכלכליות ושאר האסונות שפקדו את הארץ. כולל את השורה: "יש להתייחס לאומה (אלאמה) בעדינות, כשם שמתייחסים בעדינות לאדם חולה" (שורה 23 בצד ההפוך).
